conclusion: A fixed builtin-only Podman/shell/psql readonly bridge is an implementation choice within 80ea readonlyPG authority. It replaces transport only, adds no caller SQL/client/callback or public CLI, and does not claim any stopped Linux vendor closure was verified.
fixedBoundary: Use the original rootless /usr/bin/podman, exact existing CID/image/uid/volume/mount/port predicates. The archived original Containerfile builds PostgreSQL15.12 with --prefix=/opt/pgsql; the psql role is fixed /opt/pgsql/bin/psql, never /usr/bin/psql or PATH lookup. Actual executable/image checks remain later G2 prerequisites.

Use only reviewed fixed shell and psql argv. Disable psql startup configuration and password prompts and enforce ON_ERROR_STOP. Never expose a general SQL/query/psql method or accept caller scripts, connection strings, environment overrides or client objects.

Deliver the credential from the Node parent only over stdin to the fixed private shell wrapper; consume it before SQL and supply it only to the psql child credential environment. Never include it in argv, SQL, echo, logs, command receipts or errors. -W is not a declared stdin password protocol.

Each full per-database observation must keep all guard/catalog/row queries in one backend connection and one original REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction, with default_transaction_read_only=on and real SHOW results verified inside it. No per-query process/connection substitution, reconnect or cross-database atomicity claim.

Keep original fixed SQL, table inventory139 per DB, ordering, columns, PostgreSQL text/raw representation, xmin, PK/cells, meta/catalog/DDL/roles/sequences/marker/OIDs/M98/objects and exact snapshot8/row5 result shapes. A transport JSON envelope is acceptable only if the inner raw strings and all original pg.rows types and null/array/number/string distinctions are retained.

Only confirmed complete output and committed readonly transactions may become complete snapshot/ROG11/E9 facts. Timeout, truncation, malformed framing, uncertain exit or lost COMMIT acknowledgement stays failed/UNKNOWN, preserves existing outputs and primary evidence, and never silently re-samples or restarts services.
requiredCodeEvidence: Complete candidate module with owned fake process/stdin/stdout fixtures proves one-connection lifetime, exact argv, no secret in argv/log/error, actual SHOW before reads and no callback/client escape.
Round-trip fixtures cover empty/nonempty rows, NULL, arrays, booleans, integers/text OIDs, Unicode, quotes/newlines and exact raw/xmin/cells ordering against original capture/comparison functions.
Partial output, command error, duplicate/missing/end framing and secondary receipt failures preserve true uncertainty. Code qualification and exact actual G2 remain separate.

officialBasis.supports: psql -X disables startup files; -w avoids password prompts; ON_ERROR_STOP stops script processing with error status.
PGPASSWORD and PGOPTIONS supply libpq connection password and options; credentials remain private child state.
REPEATABLE READ visibility belongs to the current transaction and READ ONLY mode must be established before its reads.
row_to_json preserves composite structure while SQL text values remain escaped JSON strings; exact transport shape still requires qualification.

limits: No container, psql, P, proc/env, SQL/HTTP or WSL was executed or inspected. This finite contract review is for the named Root technical G3 checkpoint only; it is not code-ready or actual-data conservation evidence.
